summary.text: A 75-year-old woman consulted a Memory Clinic in 2015 because of forgetfulness that began about three months earlier. She also had increasing inner restlessness and a fear of having dementia, for which her GP prescribed citalopram 20 mg. She had thyroid disease and hypertension, an unclear alcohol history with differing third-party accounts, and reported driving confidently without accidents, avoiding night driving and preferring shorter distances.

At the first consultation she had evident short-term memory deficits and irritability, objective orientation screening showed no abnormalities, and neurological examination was unremarkable. Mental state examination found no pathological findings except prolonged loneliness, and formal criteria for depression were not fulfilled. The working diagnosis was mild cognitive impairment. Extensive neuropsychological testing showed an MMSE of 23, poor episodic memory, slow processing speed and impaired cognitive flexibility, with unimpaired semantic memory and spatial abilities.

The neuropsychologist advised her to refrain from driving until the next consultation, which was scheduled earlier, but just prior to that appointment she drove the wrong way down a one-way street and missed it. Medical confidentiality prevented the team from passing the results to her daughter or officials. At the rescheduled meeting they advised against further driving; at a social worker home visit she reported she had continued to drive short distances.

MRI showed patchy bi-hemispheric microangiopathic and lacunar lesions without more than age-appropriate atrophy. Routine CSF tests were normal, while the CSF markers for neurodegenerative disease were reported as pathological, including the beta-amyloid ratio. A consensus conference formally diagnosed mild Alzheimer’s dementia, with microangiopathy not judged the leading cause. She was informed of the diagnosis, advised to reduce drinking and given mobility advice, a cholinesterase inhibitor was proposed, and she has since consented to stop driving.

ambiguities.issue: The alcohol history is called unclear by the authors: the patient reports stopping relevant drinking four months ago and recently drinking one glass of beer per week, the partner never noticed increased consumption, and the daughter suggests regular consumption with unclear amounts. Third-party accounts are contradictory and unsubstantiated.

evidence.quote: There is an unclear history of drinking alcohol
suggests regular alcohol consumption (unclear amounts)
Third-party history was somewhat contradictory

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer alcohol use disorder, current heavy drinking or drunk driving.

ambiguities.issue: The CSF beta-amyloid 1–42 value (849 pg/mL) is called normal while the printed cut-off reads ≤450 pg/mL; the cut-off direction as printed does not match a normal value. The text then states the neurodegeneration markers were pathological without classifying total tau and phosphorylated tau individually.

evidence.quote: β-amyloid 1–42was normal (849 pg/mL cut-off: ≤450 pg/mL)
The markers for neurodegenerative disease were, however, pathological.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not reconcile the cut-off, recompute flags or assign high/low flags to the tau values.

ambiguities.issue: Two different time frames are given for the neuropsychologist’s advice to refrain from driving: until the next consultation with the physician, and (in the discussion) until the more complete work-up would provide a definite diagnosis.

evidence.quote: until the next consultation with the physician
until the more complete work-up would provide a definite diagnosis

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not merge the two durations into one stated interval, and do not treat the discussion sentence as identifying the neuropsychologist advice event or ordering it after the test.

ambiguities.issue: The authors give an alternative explanation for the wrong-way driving event (stress before the visit) but chose to interpret it as decompensation under underlying cognitive disability. The event itself was relayed by a caller to the daughter.

evidence.quote: An alternative explanation for this singular event
We, however, opted to interpret it as showing that additional stress leads to decompensation given underlying cognitive disabilities.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assert a cause of the driving event or that it was caused by dementia.

ambiguities.issue: The authors’ first-consultation summary lists slight subjective orientation difficulties, whereas the patient history states she did not report difficulties with spatial orientation. These are different wordings (general orientation vs spatial orientation) and are not treated as a source conflict.

evidence.quote: slight subjective orientation difficulties
She did not report difficulties with spatial orientation, sleep, appetite or motivation.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not merge orientation and spatial orientation into one fact.

ambiguities.issue: The statement that the authors opted to wait is an answer to a rhetorical either/or question, while another paragraph says driving safety was brought up at this stage in a preliminary manner.

evidence.quote: In the case of Mrs. L., we opted to wait.
We brought up the topic of driving safety at this stage of consultation, but it naturally was subject to preliminary evidence.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer exactly what was deferred or when driving was first discussed.

ambiguities.issue: The authors propose a cholinesterase inhibitor and report that the patient was willing to be medicated; no drug name, start or administration is reported.

evidence.quote: we proposed initiating treatment with a cholinesterase inhibitor
was willing to be medicated

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not record a medication as started or administered.

ambiguities.issue: The text says the clinic does not routinely perform hippocampal volumetry; it does not state whether it was done for this patient. Generic workflow statements and general advice to drivers (second opinion at driving schools or road safety agencies, insurance cover) are not assigned to this patient.

evidence.quote: We do not routinely perform manual or automated hippocampal volumetry.
To help drivers accept our advice to stop driving, we also provided information to seek second opinion on their driving performance

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not infer a volumetry result or that second-opinion testing was arranged for this patient.

ambiguities.issue: Table 1 prints the z-Score of the digit-span row with a decimal comma (0,1), lists a VLMT–D1 word span test that the methods text does not describe, and uses words (impaired, not impaired, normal mood, slightly depressive) in the z-Score column of some rows. The VLMT–D1 row prints the same raw score and z-Score (3, −1.3) as the RAVLT trial 1 row; the two rows are kept separate as printed.

evidence.quote: repeating numbers forward | 6 | 0,1
word span | VLMT–D1 | 3 | −1.3

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not convert the decimal comma, infer VLMT details or invent z-scores for the word-valued rows.

ambiguities.issue: The speaker of the outcome sentences changes between the case narrative and the discussion; discussion sentences naming the patient or Mrs. L. were assigned to the single index patient, while generic discussion sentences were not.

evidence.quote: In addition, Mrs. L. showed a reduced MMSE performance, a reduced driving range and reported increased irritability.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not assign general discussion statements about drivers with dementia to this patient.

ambiguities.issue: Several course steps have no literal order: the social worker home visit "three weeks later" is separated from the rescheduled advice by two generic sentences; "After all, diagnostic information was available" is punctuated as "After all," and names no test, so it does not order the neuropsychological examination, MRI or CSF analysis before the formal diagnosis; and the discussion sentence "Latter results especially prompted us to advise" is not identified as the neuropsychologist advice event.

evidence.quote: when our social worker visited the patient at home three weeks later
After all, diagnostic information was available, it was concluded that Mrs. L. should be formally diagnosed with mild Alzheimer’s Dementia.
Latter results especially prompted us to advise the patient to refrain from further driving until the more complete work-up would provide a definite diagnosis.

ambiguities.must_not_infer: Do not order these pairs from paragraph position or clinical expectation.

article_limitations: The article has no figures and no supplements; no visual, figure-EHR privacy content or supplement review applies.
Table 1 is a single-time neuropsychological result table, not a serial table; each row is one observation with its raw score and z-Score column text, units only where the source prints them.
Third-party accounts (partner, daughter, caller) are contradictory or hearsay and are recorded with that provenance; alcohol facts from third parties are review_only.
Cohort, literature and policy statements in the introduction and discussion are not assigned to the patient.
No medication was started for the dementia: a cholinesterase inhibitor was only proposed.
